Cost of adding a fourth or fifth person to one account
dimensions.a: Nothing — price is set only by active-profile count, with no seat limit at any tier
dimensions.b: Forces an upgrade — Essentials caps at 3 seats and Standard at 5; only Premium removes the limit

dimensions.label: SMS marketing
dimensions.a: Native and usage-priced: $0.01 per US toll-free segment sent, carrier fees included
dimensions.b: A separate add-on with no published flat rate; needs an application and a monthly credit purchase

dimensions.label: Ecommerce-specific features
dimensions.a: Flows read Shopify/WooCommerce order and browsing history; a Reviews add-on ($25/mo, up to 250 orders) is scoped to store order volume
dimensions.b: Purchase-behavior tracking and product recommendations included on every plan, including Free, but no Shopify- or WooCommerce-specific add-on

dimensions.label: Annual pre-pay discount
dimensions.a: None — every self-serve plan bills monthly only, with no annual toggle on the pricing page
dimensions.b: About 15% off, available on Premium at every tier and on Essentials/Standard once contacts pass 10,000

dimensions.label: Free trial of a paid plan
dimensions.a: None — a free-forever 250-profile plan stands in for a trial
dimensions.b: 14-day self-serve trial on Essentials and Standard, credit card required at signup

dimensions.label: What happens when you outgrow your current tier
dimensions.a: Automatic move to the next profile-compliant tier at its published price, whether you opted in or not
dimensions.b: An overage charge applies, but its per-contact or per-email rate isn't published on the pricing or comparison pages

dimensions.label: Paid support beyond what's included
dimensions.a: Professional support from $500/mo and Enterprise support from $1,800/mo, both needing a sales quote
dimensions.b: Scales with plan instead of a separate purchase: 24/7 chat on Essentials/Standard, phone support and a dedicated onboarding specialist on Premium

dimensions.label: Free-plan ceiling
dimensions.a: 250 active profiles, 500 emails/month, plus a monthly Composer AI and mobile-messaging usage allowance included at no charge; email support for 60 days
dimensions.b: 250 contacts, 500 emails/month (or 250/day), no automation flows or AI features; email support for 30 days only

dimensions.b: Founded in 2001; now operates as Intuit Mailchimp

verdicts.why: Klaviyo charges nothing extra as more of an agency's staff log into one client's account, while Mailchimp's seat caps can force a pricier plan regardless of that client's actual list size.

A course creator's list rarely comes from Shopify or WooCommerce order data, so Klaviyo's ecommerce-scoped add-ons go mostly unused while Mailchimp's cheaper entry plan covers the same launch and newsletter emails.
Klaviyo's flows are built directly on Shopify and WooCommerce order and browsing history, with an order-volume-priced Reviews add-on that Mailchimp has no equivalent for.
A business selling appointments rather than a product catalog gets little from Klaviyo's ecommerce integrations and pays less on Mailchimp for the same reminder and newsletter emails.
At solo-operator list sizes Mailchimp's entry plan costs less than Klaviyo's, and a service freelancer rarely has the Shopify or WooCommerce catalog Klaviyo's add-ons are built around.
An early-stage startup's list is small and not tied to ecommerce orders, so Mailchimp's lower entry price matters more than Klaviyo's Shopify- and WooCommerce-specific features.
